children: First Solar (FSLR) was among the biggest decliners, losing 10.3% and reaching a fresh 52-week low. Sunrun
dropped 6.8%, while Eos Energy Enterprises (EOSE) shed 9.3%. SolarEdge Technologies
and Canadian Solar (CSIQ) also posted declines.

Bond-market conditions were a central factor. The 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.48%, its highest level since 2004, while the 10-year yield climbed to 5.2%. Higher yields can raise the expense of financing large energy projects and affect their expected returns.

The broader rate move followed concerns about inflation and government spending, while recent economic data pointed to continued U.S. activity. Those factors have added pressure to longer-term borrowing costs.

Renewable-energy policy also remained uncertain. Bloomberg reported that administration officials could withdraw an offer involving delayed wind and solar projects if negotiations over permitting legislation fail to advance, potentially leaving some developments in limbo.

title: Solar Stocks Tumble After 30-Year Treasury Yield Hits 2004 High
